independent_utility_rule: A Toki Pona gap becomes a Pictiq candidate only if the concept would materially improve Pictiq even if the Toki Pona crosswalk did not exist.

communication_mode_method.rule: Use the body for what the body can express. Use the icon for what must remain after the body is gone.
communication_mode_method.counting_unit: Each state count is the number of distinct source NONE words or candidate concepts tagged with that state. States may overlap.

states.EMBODIED-OMITTABLE: A present person, visible referent, gesture, gaze, voice, or shared situation can reliably supply the concept for the embodied use.
states.STANDALONE-GAP: The concept must survive in an unattended or remote artifact and existing Pictiq tiles or honest composition do not preserve it.
states.OUT-OF-SCOPE: Explicit encoding would import language-specific grammar, excessive lexical breadth, or a concept without independent Pictiq utility.

communication_mode_method.finding: NONE is not a single failure state: embodiment may supply a concept, standalone use may expose a need, or the concept may be outside Pictiq scope.

semantic_review.why_review: The only COMPOSED row; shop plus cash clearly signals practical commerce but narrows barter and exchange.
semantic_review.alternative: CONTEXTUAL for a shopping scene; PARTIAL with place_shop; NONE for abstract exchange.

semantic_review.why_review: Urgency is only one possible emotional force and can overstate neutral emphasis.
logic_no expresses rejection only when the situation supplies the evaluated quality.
logic_yes answers a permission question but does not represent ability or possibility.
A hotel suggests sleep only in a travel or lodging context.
semantic_review.alternative: NONE outside a known lodging use case.

semantic_review.why_review: Beer suggests only one possible cause of intoxication and risks a misleading stereotype.
Urgency may reinforce a command but is not a general imperative or vocative marker.
semantic_review.alternative: NONE; rely on pointing and interaction.

semantic_review.why_review: A repair tile can imply a broken object, but only within an operational scene.
semantic_review.alternative: NONE for harm or mistake senses.

semantic_review.why_review: logic_no can mean closed or stopped, while completion and past remain absent.
semantic_review.alternative: PARTIAL if the closed/stopped protocol sense is treated as stable.

semantic_review.why_review: logic_yes communicates approval or OK only within an exchange.
need_water is an explicit example of need-intent, not a representation of broad desire.
A flower is a recognizable plant subtype but covers only a narrow part of the field.
semantic_review.alternative: NONE if subtype overlap is judged too narrow.

semantic_review.why_review: need_food is broader and intent-bearing, but the edible-object overlap is useful.

semantic_review.meaning: fun, play, game, art or entertainment
semantic_review.why_review: A disco is one venue and activity; it does not represent general fun, play or art.

semantic_review.meaning: many, several, quantity, very or twenty
semantic_review.why_review: qty_5 can pragmatically signal many but still depicts a specific number.
semantic_review.alternative: COMPOSED qty_5 + qty_plus for an explicit many expression.

semantic_review.meaning: begin, start, open or turn on
semantic_review.why_review: logic_yes has a stable open reading but misses beginning and activation broadly.
need_food is much broader and carries need intent, but includes the central edible field.
love_heart covers affection only, leaving physical sensation and most emotions outside.
semantic_review.alternative: NONE if affection is too narrow to count as useful overlap.

semantic_review.meaning: communication, speech, thought, story or language
semantic_review.why_review: A phone is a channel/device for one communication mode, not communication itself.
A condom is a related protection object, creating contextual association rather than semantic overlap.
A power outlet represents access to electricity, not power or strength generally.
semantic_review.alternative: CONTEXTUAL for electrical-power requests; NONE generally.

candidate_clusters.name: people and social roles
candidate_clusters.concepts: neutral person, group, parent/caretaker and gendered roles
candidate_clusters.workaround: Pointing and conversational context; no generic person tile.
candidate_clusters.note: Advance only a neutral person concept; do not infer separate role or gender tiles.

candidate_clusters.name: pronouns and deixis
candidate_clusters.concepts: I/we, this/that, third person and you
candidate_clusters.workaround: Pointing, speaker roles and surrounding context.
candidate_clusters.note: Lexical pronoun tiles would add grammar that Pictiq currently avoids.

candidate_clusters.name: body, perception and clothing
candidate_clusters.concepts: hearing, clothing, sight, body, skin and mouth
candidate_clusters.workaround: safety_medical for help; place_fashion_shopping only for retail clothing.
candidate_clusters.note: Eye/attention, basic clothing and body-location concepts need separate use-case tests.

candidate_clusters.name: buildings, places and surfaces
candidate_clusters.concepts: opening, land/place, horizontal surface and building/home
candidate_clusters.workaround: Specific hotel, shop, park, airport and landmark tiles.
candidate_clusters.note: Generic building/home is strong; the other concepts remain unproven.

candidate_clusters.name: spatial relations and orientation
candidate_clusters.concepts: below, inside, behind, beside, above and front
candidate_clusters.workaround: Physical arrangement, pointing and layout position.
candidate_clusters.note: A directional system would require independent protocol research.

candidate_clusters.name: animals
candidate_clusters.concepts: reptiles, fish, insects, land animals and birds
candidate_clusters.workaround: No generic animal tile; use the visible referent when present.
candidate_clusters.note: Test a generic animal/wildlife need before taxonomic icon work.

candidate_clusters.name: everyday objects and documents
candidate_clusters.workaround: Point to the object; existing money_card is payment-specific.
candidate_clusters.note: Container or document may be useful, but generic thing is too unspecific.

candidate_clusters.name: materials and geometric forms
candidate_clusters.concepts: hard material, semi-solid, flexible line, rigid rod and round form
candidate_clusters.note: No shared candidate follows from these broad material bundles.

candidate_clusters.name: environment, sky and light
candidate_clusters.workaround: No generic environmental tile; physical context may supply the referent.
candidate_clusters.note: Light/visibility is more practical than copying the full lexical fields.

candidate_clusters.name: temperature, physical state and danger
candidate_clusters.concepts: unclean/toxic, cold, death, heat/fire and conflict
candidate_clusters.workaround: safety_medical or safety_police only for requesting help after a problem.
candidate_clusters.note: Hot/fire and cold warrant tests; help tiles do not represent the underlying states.

candidate_clusters.name: colors and visual appearance
candidate_clusters.concepts: color category plus yellow, blue/green, red, dark and light
candidate_clusters.workaround: Point to a visible color or use the colored object itself.
candidate_clusters.note: Evaluate a compact modifier system rather than unrelated noun-like icons.

candidate_clusters.name: communication and cognition
candidate_clusters.concepts: interjection/emphasis, sound, vocalization, name/word, image/writing and knowledge
candidate_clusters.workaround: comm_phone and comm_wifi cover specific channels, not these concepts.
candidate_clusters.note: A message/communication concept may be useful; abstract cognition remains low priority.

candidate_clusters.name: actions, change and movement
candidate_clusters.concepts: search, change, wait, arrive, method/path, give, repeat and remove
candidate_clusters.workaround: Situational context and concrete object/transport tiles.
candidate_clusters.note: Test concrete actions from product scenarios instead of importing broad verbs.

candidate_clusters.name: grammar and abstract relations
candidate_clusters.concepts: coordination, argument marking, instrument, context, location, comparison, cause, vocative and imperative grammar
candidate_clusters.workaround: Tile order, layout, pointing and natural-language context.
candidate_clusters.note: These would make Pictiq unnecessarily grammatical or import extreme polysemy.

candidate_clusters.name: size and abstract quantity
candidate_clusters.workaround: Existing qty_1, qty_2, qty_5, qty_plus and qty_minus express concrete quantities.
candidate_clusters.note: Only large/small modifiers merit testing; do not import age, importance or totality.

candidate_clusters.name: possession and containment relation
candidate_clusters.workaround: Physical possession, pointing and adjacent object context.
candidate_clusters.note: A generic possession operator would expand Pictiq grammar without demonstrated demand.

candidate_clusters.name: polysemous abstract qualities
candidate_clusters.workaround: Use concrete people, institutions, foods or situations when available.
candidate_clusters.note: Each word bundles unrelated concepts that should not become one tile.

candidate_clusters.name: Toki Pona-specific culture
candidate_clusters.concepts: interaction with the official Toki Pona book
candidate_clusters.workaround: Text or a specific book reference outside the protocol.
candidate_clusters.note: The concept has no independent Pictiq utility.

candidate_concepts.role: neutral participant for travel, safety and interpersonal composition
candidate_concepts.mode_reason: Pointing can identify a participant live; a durable safety or travel artifact may still require a neutral person.

candidate_concepts.role: generic shelter/destination distinct from named venue types
candidate_concepts.workaround: specific hotel, shop, airport and landmark tiles
candidate_concepts.mode_reason: A visible building can be indicated live; an unattended destination or shelter message needs the generic concept to remain.

candidate_concepts.role: look/see cue for accessibility and signage
candidate_concepts.mode_reason: Gaze and pointing work live; an accessibility or attention cue must encode the concept when unattended.
Visible clothing can be pointed to; remote packing or identification instructions may need an explicit object concept.

candidate_concepts.workaround: safety_medical requests help without locating the issue
candidate_concepts.mode_reason: A person can indicate a body location live; a stored medical message must preserve where the issue is.
Heat is not reliably visible or gestureable, and warnings must remain understandable without a communicator.
Cold is not reliably visible or gestureable, and comfort or safety instructions can outlast the exchange.
Relative scale can be demonstrated live; remote selection instructions may need size encoded.

candidate_concepts.workaround: point to colors or colored objects
candidate_concepts.mode_reason: A visible color can be pointed to live; remote object identification needs the color to survive in the artifact.
Voice, phone, or a note can supply the channel live; a channel-neutral interface cue may need an explicit message concept.

candidate_concepts.role: lighting, visibility, or access cue distinct from a celestial-body reading
candidate_concepts.workaround: ambient context or pointing works only when the communicator and condition are present
candidate_concepts.mode_reason: Ambient light can be indicated live; an unattended visibility, lighting, or access instruction may need it encoded.
The physical container is usually pointable; standalone demand remains unproven, so keep the proposal deferred.
A visible animal can be indicated directly; standalone warning demand remains too broad and unproven.

candidate_concepts.workaround: neutral person, pointing and conversational roles
candidate_concepts.mode_reason: Speaker roles, pointing, and a neutral person can supply participants; grammatical person and gender are outside current scope.

candidate_concepts.role: copy Toki Pona syntax into tiles
candidate_concepts.mode_reason: These operators would copy language-specific syntax rather than solve an independently demonstrated Pictiq task.

safe_none_groups.name: grammar, possession and language-specific abstraction
safe_none_groups.reason: These concepts add grammar, copy Toki Pona-specific structure or collapse unrelated senses.

safe_none_groups.name: pronoun, gender and social-role distinctions
safe_none_groups.reason: A neutral person candidate can be tested separately; individual role and pronoun tiles have no demonstrated demand.

safe_none_groups.name: broad action and spatial vocabulary
safe_none_groups.reason: Concrete situations, pointing and layout should remain the default until a recurring Pictiq task proves a gap.

safe_none_groups.name: under-evidenced physical and nature taxonomies
safe_none_groups.reason: Possible concepts require product evidence; the source words remain safely NONE meanwhile.

safe_none_groups.name: candidate-bearing modifier and accessibility areas
safe_none_groups.reason: Concept-level proposals are review prompts, not reasons to change any current NONE row.

resolution.context: Final acceptance of the complete 120-word Toki Pona to Pictiq interoperability crosswalk.

accepted_architecture.entity_symbol_finding: Proper names expose a scoped entity-symbol mechanism: a narrative pack may assign local visual identifiers to entities such as Odysseus, Penelope, and Telemachus without adding lexical Core tiles.
accepted_architecture.parametric_color_finding: Embodied use can point to an actual color; standalone use may carry an arbitrary color value in a proposed parametric tile. Individual lexical color icons are rejected.
